summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 111% to INR 45,484 million, but Q4 EBITDA margin compressed sharply on input-cost inflation and rupee depreciation.
summary.overview: Saatvik reported record FY26 revenue of INR 45,484 million (up about 111% YoY), EBITDA of INR 5,811 million (12.78% margin) and PAT of INR 3,571 million (7.85% margin). Q4 revenue hit a record INR 16,077 million, but EBITDA fell to INR 1,166 million and PAT to INR 604 million, as silver, aluminium, copper and oil-linked input costs rose and the rupee weakened after the war that began 20 February 2026. Management said fixed-price contracts could not pass on these increases immediately. Cell capacity expansion is the main near-term story: 2.4 GW cell line is targeted to start production in H2 FY27, and the cell plan is now 6 GW.

financial_highlights.change: decline; margin compressed (Q4 margin cited as about 7% by analyst)

segments.name: Solar modules and cells (core)
segments.commentary: FY26 production 3,162 MW (FY25: 1,459 MW) and sales 3,138 MW (FY25: 1,389 MW); capacity utilisation over 84%. Confirmed order book about 5.89 GW (about INR 8,000 crore) as of March 2026.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: FY26 EPC contribution about 150 MW, about 3-4% of revenue/profit; FY27 expected in same range. Solar pump EPC about INR 50 crore (about 1% of top line).

segments.name: Encapsulant (EPE)
segments.commentary: 2 GW Ambala facility commissioned in FY26; expansion roadmap raised to 5 GW. Management cites 5-10% savings versus external sourcing and about 80% utilisation expected.

segments.name: Transformers, inverters, storage and others
segments.commentary: 80% stake acquired in Melcon Transformers and Electricals; UDAY on-grid inverter series launched; Saatvik Power Storage Solutions formed for BESS. No financials disclosed for these.

guidance_outlook: Management said FY27 margins should be stable and healthy, with a return toward the previously seen level (about 15% was raised by an analyst) but declined to give a number.
Q1 FY27 expected to be softer due to war-driven volatility in USD, commodities and oil; cell-linked margin improvement expected in H2 FY27.
2.4 GW cell line: module equipment move-in from June 2026, cell equipment move-in from July 2026, production start in H2 FY27 (G12R line).
Phase II cell capacity raised from 2.4 GW to 3.6 GW with civil work from August 2026; total 6 GW cell capacity targeted around June-July 2027.
Ingot and wafer entry planned at 6 GW; capex about INR 2,500 crore in total, about INR 1,800-2,000 crore expected in FY28.
FY27 capex for expansion about INR 1,700 crore, funded by a mix of debt and equity (equity from accruals).
Debt-equity expected to stay between 1.0 and 1.5 times, not more than that.
Order book execution timeline about 18 months, with some orders at 3-12 months.
capex_capacity: 2 GW encapsulant facility in Ambala commissioned in FY26; expansion to 5 GW planned; encapsulant utilisation about 80%.
Cell capacity: 2.4 GW first phase with civil and building ready; Phase II raised to 3.6 GW, total 6 GW by around June-July 2027.
Module planned capacity cited by analyst as 8.8 GW versus 5 GW encapsulant plan; management does not intend to match them at present.
Ingot and wafer plan 6 GW, with capex in FY28.
FY27 capex about INR 1,700 crore; FY28 capex about INR 1,800-2,000 crore out of a total of about INR 2,500 crore for ingot.
demand_pricing: Order book about 5.89 GW; about 65% from large utility customers (mostly pass-through pricing) and the rest from C&I on fixed-price terms.
Q4 margin compression linked to silver, aluminium, copper, oil and rupee moves; the rupee moved from about 88 to 94 per USD after the war, a 5-6% impact on fixed-price contracts.

Management said cell demand is a seller's market, with Mono PERC in high demand from retail (PM Surya Ghar, KUSUM) and initial cell output to focus on retail before C&I and utility by end Q3 or early Q4 FY27.
Long-term contracts are structured to pass through USD, silver (wafer cost plus) and change-in-law risks, though management said some utility orders must absorb cost increases.
Management said Mono PERC is inefficient and demand is strong, and it expects some non-DCR pipeline to take 12-18 months to execute.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 EBITDA decline, and what margins do new orders carry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher silver, aluminium, copper and oil-linked costs, rupee depreciation, and fixed-price contracts signed before the war that could not be repriced immediately. Some new orders can pass costs through and others must absorb them, depending on the customer.

qa_highlights.question: When will the 2.4 GW and 6 GW cell lines start and stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Module equipment move-in starts June 2026 and cell equipment move-in July 2026, with production starting in H2 FY27. Phase II (3.6 GW) civil work starts August 2026; full 6 GW by June-July 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27-FY28 capex and debt plans?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 expansion capex is about INR 1,700 crore, funded by debt and accrual-funded equity. FY28 capex is about INR 1,800-2,000 crore for ingot. Debt-equity is expected to stay between 1.0 and 1.5 times, currently 0.65.

qa_highlights.question: Why has cash conversion been low, and why did creditor days fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Large PSU orders carry 90-120 day recovery cycles, with Q4 dispatches recovering in April-May. Creditor days normalised as the company paid suppliers faster to secure better pricing during the volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Will cells be sold externally, and what are the EPC and order-execution details?
qa_highlights.answer: The 6 GW cell capacity is currently for captive use, but management will decide on external sales based on margins. Execution timeline is about 18 months, EPC contribution is about 3-4% and stays in that range in FY27.

risks_watch: Margin compression from silver, aluminium, copper, oil and USD/INR volatility, with Q1 FY27 expected to be softer.
Execution risk on 2.4 GW cell commissioning (July 2026 equipment move-in) and stabilisation of efficiencies, given the newness of the line and the need for utility-level quality approvals.
Rising debt to fund 6 GW cells and ingot capex, with debt-equity up to 1.5x.
Weak cash conversion (about 17-18% per analyst), tied to PSU receivables of 90-120 days and lower creditor days.
ALMM-II effective date (1 June 2026 per management) and ALMM-III (June 2028, 15 GW cumulative from at least three manufacturers).
Q4 call for interim CFO; no confirmed permanent CFO was named.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and capacity build-out, but cautious and vague on near-term margins: management repeatedly declined to give numerical FY27 margin guidance and attributed Q4 weakness to the war-driven cost shock.
key_quotes: So what happens is that for us, it has been a good move, and that's the reason why we are expanding this capacity, which is one for our internal consumption and also for selling in the business.
So we'll be 6 gigawatt by somewhere around mid of -- around July -- yes, June-July 2027.
But what we see is that -- and that cell manufacturing, that revenue, and our bottom line margins will significantly improve in the second half of the year.

adds.what: 2.4 GW G12R cell line (Phase I), production start in H2 FY27
Cell Phase II expansion raised from 2.4 GW to 3.6 GW, total cell capacity 6 GW by June-July 2027
Encapsulant expansion from 2 GW Ambala to 5 GW roadmap

growth.why: Management guided FY27 margins as 'stable and healthy' without a number and Q1 FY27 as softer, while the 2.4 GW cell line (production H2 FY27) and 6 GW cell target by June-July 2027 are backed by a 5.89 GW (about INR 8,000 crore) order book and FY27 expansion capex of about INR 1,700 crore; no explicit FY27 revenue growth number was given.
